You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The unemployment rate is 8.3% with a 12m change of -0.8, so it was about 9.1% a year earlier. That fits early 2012 (8.3% in Feb 2012; 9.1% in Aug–Sep 2011 and 8.3% in Jan–Feb 2012). A 12m decline of 0.8 from Feb 2011 (8.9%) would give 8.1%, so the match is not exact. The other data point to the same period.

- The fed funds rate of 0.14% fits 2012.
- The 10-year yield of 1.63% fits March 2012 (about 2.2%) less well than it fits the end of the year. The 10-year was about 1.6% in Dec 2012, but unemployment was 7.8% then. In mid-2012 it was around 1.6% in June (unemployment 8.2%) and 1.5% in July.
- Headline CPI of 1.42% YoY fits June 2012 (1.7%) or July 2012 (1.4%). The 3m change of -0.87 fits a falling CPI path, with CPI at 2.3% in April, 1.7% in June and 1.4% in July.
- US large-cap equity returned +19.2% over 12 months and +10.8% over 3 months. That fits the 12 months to Sept 2012, when the 3m return was about 6%. It also fits the 12 months to Dec 2012, when the figure was about 16%.
- Unemployment was 8.1% in Aug 2012 and 7.8% in Sep 2012, so 8.3% points to June–July 2012. The 3m payroll average of 105k fits June–July 2012.
- The dollar was up 14.7% over 12m, which fits mid-2012 after the Euro crisis.
- Gold was +6.5% in 1m, which fits July–Aug 2012. The VIX at 17.8 down 6 over 3m, with developed ex-US equity up 4.6% in 1m, fits the Draghi rally.

Dev ex-US was +4.6% in 1m, and 3m +12.5% points to Sept 2012, with the gold 1m gain also fitting then. Gold rose about 6.5% in Sept 2012, and the 10-year was about 1.63%. Unemployment, though, was 7.8% in Sep 2012 as published then. It was later revised, and the snapshot may use the latest vintage, where unemployment was about 8.3%? Probably not. Still, the other cues point to Sep 2012.

Industrial production YoY of 4.37% was about right for Sep 2012 in the data as then published.
